liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (4 reviews): Described as slow, whisky-blurred, low-down New Orleans; Garcia shows blue-note mastery and keeps inventing new phrases through every verse; Reviewer praises Iko Iko and Garcia's blues picking [9][12][14][18]
- **Scarlet Begonias** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the Scarlet-Fire top five, with a smooth transition into Fire and a rousing Garcia solo at the end; Dissenting reviewer finds the segue jam aimless and unfocused, with the band out of sync apart from fleeting moments [12][13]
- **Fire On The Mountain** (1 review): Garcia's closing lead in Fire produces a couple of new, memorable melodic phrases on the major scale [9]
- **Drums** (1 review): Drums runs about twenty minutes, exploring varied themes with Mickey playing steel pans [18]

## The recordings

- **gd1978-04-11.sbd.miller.108666.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 20 songs; 168 min; rated 4.67/5 by 6 [1]
- **gd1978-04-11.sbd.miller.tetzeli.fix-18099.81257.sbeok.flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 170 min; rated 3/5 by 1 [2]
- **gd78-04-11.sbd.miller.18099.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 20 songs; 170 min; rated 3.28/5 by 18 [4]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the sound great and the playing well executed, though the first set is pedestrian; Reviewer notes vocals are quite good, with Donna not spoiling anything, and Garcia is fully engaged [18][20]
- **gd1978-04-11.150607.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: soundboard; 20 songs; 169 min [5]. Said about its sound: Source has proper stereo imaging; start of Friend Of The Devil is clipped on all sources; A reel change cuts the very end of Terrapin on all circulating sources [5]
- **gd1978-04-11.157654.aud.hicks-fong.flac2448**: audience recording; 20 songs; 152 min [6]. Said about its sound: Some tracks begin abruptly as the deck was switched on; Drums starts after a tape flip and lacks its end [6]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first Southern show; recalls polite ushers and a ceiling resembling a display of the Solar System [14]
- Recalls Garcia and others tinkering on steel drums stage right during Drums [14]
- Reviewer counts this Scarlet>Fire among their favorites of all versions heard, while finding the rest of the set dull [11]
- Reviewer found the show's feeling a contrast to the band's vibe one year earlier [15]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1978-04-11.sbd.miller.108666.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat (44.1k) [1]. Also: This transfer was made with much better gear than the uploader's earlier transfer [1]
- **gd1978-04-11.sbd.miller.tetzeli.fix-18099.81257.sbeok.flac16**: transferred by Seamless fix of shnid 18099 by Bill Tetzeli; source: SBD -> Rm -> PCM -> Dat [2]. Also: A 16-second redundancy between discs 2 and 3 was removed for a seamless transition; SHN files converted to FLAC [2]
- **gd78-04-11.sbd.miller.18099.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: Soundboard [4]
- **gd1978-04-11.150607.BettyBoard.Anon.Noel.t-flac16**: taped by Betty Cantor; transferred by DAT Source & Transfer by Anonymous Edited & Mastered by Joe Noel May 17, 2020; source: Betty Cantor's Master SBD Reel > PCM > DAT [5]. Also: Betty Board source shared anonymously; emphasis turned off and DC offset removed [5]
- **gd1978-04-11.157654.aud.hicks-fong.flac2448**: taped by concert recording by John Hicks & Dennis Fong; transferred by Transferred by Andrew F. 08/2022; source: Handheld deck (mono) > Maxell XLII [6]. Also: Audience recording, possibly on a portable Panasonic held at head level, per John Hicks-Fong's recollection [6]
